incomplete_derived_links.scope: Dietary folate, including folic acid reduced by dihydrofolate reductase, is converted through the folate cycle to 5-methyltetrahydrofolate, the methyl donor used by methionine synthase.
incomplete_derived_links.limitations: This conversion pathway does not show that increasing folate intake increases tissue remethylation flux. Folic acid lowers blood homocysteine, which is a circulating marker.

network_relationships.route: derived intervention target; not direct dietary admission
network_relationships.limitation: The C8 acyl form is not free octanoate content in food. Mixed-chain MCT products have formulation-dependent composition. This is a multireaction biological process, not a single chemical reaction. Tissue partitioning and energy state prevent a fixed food-to-acetyl-CoA yield. Cofactor participation creates no separate dietary admissions. The endogenous product can interconvert with beta-hydroxybutyrate, but the target identity here is acetoacetate. Ketogenesis, cerebral uptake and ATP production are distinct; no fixed yield or universal benefit is inferred.

canonical_relationships.scope: Arginine supplies a co-substrate for AGAT-dependent guanidinoacetate formation, followed by GAMT-dependent creatine production.
canonical_relationships.limitations: Capacity of the endogenous synthesis route is distinct from a claim that extra amino-acid intake raises cerebral creatine, phosphocreatine buffering or cognition. AGAT feedback, GAMT methyl supply, organ exchange and SLC6A8-mediated tissue transport constrain delivery. Human renal GAA production is not a measurement of brain synthesis flux; rat arginine infusion and glycine null responses are not oral human efficacy experiments.

canonical_relationships.scope: Betaine donates methyl groups through [BRS2 PM2 — BHMT remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm2-betaine-bhmt-remethylation), predominantly in liver and kidney, replenishing methionine upstream of [BRS2 PM3 — SAM synthesis](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm3-same-synthesis). SAM is used by COMT during dopamine metabolism.
canonical_relationships.limitations: This is peripheral BHMT supply, not neuronal BHMT activity or measured delivery into neural SAM. Dietary methionine and folate remethylation provide alternatives. Homocysteine lowering does not establish regional clearance, a limiting constraint or benefit from extra intake.

canonical_relationships.scope: Betaine donates methyl groups through [BRS2 PM2 — BHMT remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm2-betaine-bhmt-remethylation), predominantly in liver and kidney, replenishing methionine upstream of [BRS2 PM3 — SAM synthesis](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm3-same-synthesis). SAM is used by COMT during noradrenaline metabolism.
canonical_relationships.limitations: This is peripheral BHMT supply, not neuronal BHMT activity or measured delivery into neural SAM. Dietary methionine and folate remethylation provide alternatives. Homocysteine lowering does not establish regional clearance, a limiting constraint or benefit from extra intake.

canonical_relationships.scope: Betaine donates a methyl group through hepatic [BRS2 PM2 — BHMT remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm2-betaine-bhmt-remethylation), replenishing methionine/SAM used by [BRS2 PM7 — PEMT formation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm3/brs2-fm3-pm7-phosphatidylcholine-formation) upstream of DHA-bearing LPC carrier delivery.
canonical_relationships.limitations: Supported biochemical supply chain, not a demonstrated increase in net adult brain DHA incorporation. Folate/choline compensation, hepatic BHMT, SAM turnover and carrier remodelling vary by context. Mouse folate effects were sex/tissue dependent; betaine rescue used ethanol-exposed rats. The downstream human tracer study administered choline, not folate or betaine. A donor-specific limiting effect and extra-intake benefit remain unresolved.

canonical_relationships.scope: Methyl-donor substrate for BHMT remethylation of homocysteine to methionine
canonical_relationships.limitations: Supplemental betaine lowers plasma homocysteine in healthy adults, but that change does not measure tissue BHMT activity or show a clinical benefit. Human evidence is an eight-man depletion pilot, with the challenge response in four clinically depleted participants; tissue BHMT flux was not measured. Rat donor rescue and specific inhibition support the chain. This does not establish ordinary-diet limitation, response in every tissue or benefit above adequacy. Folate’s indirect constraint on BHMT remains unresolved.

canonical_relationships.scope: Sulfur-amino-acid substrate joined to glutamate in the first ATP-dependent step of glutathione assembly.
canonical_relationships.limitations: Cysteine is the substrate of the first assembly step. A formula that removed methionine and cysteine together slowed whole-blood synthesis, and that formula also removed methionine. When methionine intake stayed adequate, removing cysteine did not lower red-cell synthesis in young men. This does not show that eating more cysteine, once intake is adequate, raises glutathione synthesis.

canonical_relationships.scope: Cysteine supplies a constituent of glutathione. Glutathione participates in the redox regulation of NF-κB kinase activity and DNA binding; this is upstream resource supply, not a direct NF-κB reaction substrate.
canonical_relationships.limitations: This is supported upstream supply, not a demonstrated dietary constraint on NF-κB. Human precursor supplementation measured red-cell glutathione, not NF-κB; cysteine was supplied as N-acetylcysteine together with glycine. Cellular redox studies show context-dependent effects, including inhibition after glutathione depletion or increased extracellular cysteine. Neither individual dietary limitation, brain transfer nor benefit from additional intake is established.

canonical_relationships.scope: Cysteine supplies a constituent of glutathione used in epithelial redox protection. Glutathione prevented oxidant-induced paracellular permeability in a cell model; this supports upstream supply to a barrier-protection route, not a proven dietary reduction in endotoxin spillover.
canonical_relationships.limitations: Supported upstream supply through glutathione-dependent epithelial redox protection, not an established dietary constraint on endotoxin spillover. Human precursor tracing measured red-cell glutathione after combined glycine and N-acetylcysteine; epithelial experiments measured oxidant-induced paracellular permeability. In Salmonella-infected rats, glutathione depletion did not increase permeability or bacterial translocation. Neither intestinal precursor inadequacy, individual constituent limitation, human LPS reduction nor benefit from additional intake is established.

incomplete_derived_links.scope: Dietary methionine can supply cysteine for glutathione assembly. Methionine is not a substrate of the assembly enzymes.
incomplete_derived_links.limitations: A formula that removed methionine and cysteine together slowed whole-blood synthesis, so that result does not isolate methionine. In the cysteine-free study, methionine intake stayed adequate and red-cell synthesis did not fall. This does not show that eating more methionine, once intake is adequate, raises glutathione synthesis.

incomplete_derived_links.scope: Supplemental cysteine precursor given with glycine to older adults, in whom erythrocyte glutathione synthesis increased.
incomplete_derived_links.limitations: The synthesis increase was measured in older adults given this precursor together with glycine. It does not show an effect of N-acetylcysteine alone, of ordinary foods, or of supplementation outside that group, and it is not a neuronal or clinical result.

canonical_relationships.scope: Long-chain omega-3 fatty acid incorporated into neuronal-membrane phospholipids
canonical_relationships.limitations: Diet can provide DHA for membrane incorporation. That does not establish an ADHD treatment effect or a human dosing rule from the porcine phospholipid comparison.

canonical_relationships.scope: DHA supplementation increased hippocampal dendritic spine density in adult gerbils in the studied four-week exposure.
canonical_relationships.limitations: This is a preclinical structural state response, not proof of an indispensable intake or verified new synapse counts. It does not establish human synapse growth, ordinary-food equivalence or cognitive benefit. Developmental mouse marker and visual-response evidence is additional, context-specific support; marker abundance is not an ultrastructurally verified contact count.

canonical_relationships.scope: Defined oral DHA exposure attenuated selected post-exercise LPS-stimulated mononuclear-cell cytokine-production responses in the tested human context.
canonical_relationships.limitations: Fifteen male soccer players, eight weeks, 1.16 g DHA/day in a matched beverage comparison. Ex-vivo stimulated production is not resting circulating signalling, receptor response or universal anti-inflammatory benefit. No effect from ordinary fish portions or brain/ADHD outcome is established; temperature and exercise responses differ.

canonical_relationships.scope: n-3 fatty-acid substrate for specialised pro-resolving mediator synthesis
canonical_relationships.limitations: Five days of 2.4 g a day in healthy adults raised some pro-resolving mediators, not every mediator, and not a disease-resolution outcome.

canonical_relationships.scope: Defined oral DHA exposures can modulate circulating adiponectin, an adipose-derived endocrine signal.
canonical_relationships.limitations: Admission concerns a circulating hormone response in studied supplement/enriched-oil contexts. It does not establish adipose secretion, receptor sensitivity, universal benefit, ordinary-food efficacy or a food-effective dose. Mixture and carrier effects are not attributed to DHA alone; DHA-specific attribution uses the separate DHA-versus-EPA trial.

canonical_relationships.scope: DHA supplies the acyl chain used to form N-docosahexaenoyl-PE and synaptamide.
canonical_relationships.limitations: Labelled neural-cell precursor experiments support formation; controlled oral-oil studies support corresponding plasma ethanolamide availability. Plasma concentration is not neuronal synthesis flux or receptor engagement, and no ordinary-food effective dose or clinical benefit is established. Direct is relative to this biosynthetic operation, not direct food content of synaptamide.

106 completers from115 randomised; narrative withdrawal counts are internally inconsistent. Use flow/Results cohort sizes, not a claim of complete intention-to-treat. Whey protein is not biologically inert; authors note possible IBS sensitivity. No significant symptom exacerbation was observed in control. Permeability was secondary; no direct junction-protein or mediator measurement. Not generalisable to IBS with normal permeability, other disease types, children, pregnancy/lactation or excluded renal/hepatic impairment. No significant control-arm permeability change; adverse-event rates similar and no serious adverse events reported. Long-term safety not established. Earlier discovery shorthand0.05 versus0.11 conflated post-treatment with active-group baseline; post-treatment control was0.10, and Table3 is the actual between-group change comparison.

canonical_relationships.scope: Glycine is the acceptor substrate of glycine N-methyltransferase, which consumes SAM and forms SAH and sarcosine during methyl-group handling.
canonical_relationships.limitations: Endogenous glycine synthesis and other methyltransferases also contribute. Enzyme loss is not glycine deficiency; extra dietary glycine has not been established to normalise whole-cycle or brain methylation.

canonical_relationships.scope: Amino-acid substrate added to γ-glutamylcysteine in the second ATP-dependent step of glutathione assembly.
canonical_relationships.limitations: In older adults glycine was supplemented together with a cysteine precursor, so that rise in erythrocyte synthesis does not isolate glycine.

canonical_relationships.scope: Glycine supplies a constituent of glutathione. Glutathione participates in the redox regulation of NF-κB kinase activity and DNA binding; this is upstream resource supply, not a direct NF-κB reaction substrate.
canonical_relationships.limitations: This is supported upstream supply, not a demonstrated dietary constraint on NF-κB. Human precursor supplementation measured red-cell glutathione, not NF-κB; cysteine was supplied as N-acetylcysteine together with glycine. Cellular redox studies show context-dependent effects, including inhibition after glutathione depletion or increased extracellular cysteine. Neither individual dietary limitation, brain transfer nor benefit from additional intake is established.

canonical_relationships.scope: Glycine supplies a constituent of glutathione used in epithelial redox protection. Glutathione prevented oxidant-induced paracellular permeability in a cell model; this supports upstream supply to a barrier-protection route, not a proven dietary reduction in endotoxin spillover.
canonical_relationships.limitations: Supported upstream supply through glutathione-dependent epithelial redox protection, not an established dietary constraint on endotoxin spillover. Human precursor tracing measured red-cell glutathione after combined glycine and N-acetylcysteine; epithelial experiments measured oxidant-induced paracellular permeability. In Salmonella-infected rats, glutathione depletion did not increase permeability or bacterial translocation. Neither intestinal precursor inadequacy, individual constituent limitation, human LPS reduction nor benefit from additional intake is established.

canonical_relationships.scope: Glycine supplies a co-substrate for AGAT-dependent guanidinoacetate formation, followed by GAMT-dependent creatine production.
canonical_relationships.limitations: Capacity of the endogenous synthesis route is distinct from a claim that extra amino-acid intake raises cerebral creatine, phosphocreatine buffering or cognition. AGAT feedback, GAMT methyl supply, organ exchange and SLC6A8-mediated tissue transport constrain delivery. Human renal GAA production is not a measurement of brain synthesis flux; rat arginine infusion and glycine null responses are not oral human efficacy experiments.

canonical_relationships.scope: Coverage of the indispensable amino-acid set, including phenylalanine, that sets the circulating pool neurotransmitter pathways can draw on. Meals contribute measurable amino-acid composition; this is not a requirement that each meal provide complete coverage
canonical_relationships.limitations: Protein-quality scoring and vegetarian-diet amino-acid coverage do not establish that increasing protein raises brain monoamine synthesis or improves attention or mood. The indispensable set includes phenylalanine; tyrosine is not an indispensable amino acid.

network_relationships.limitation: Protein-quality scoring and vegetarian-diet amino-acid coverage do not establish that increasing protein raises brain monoamine synthesis or improves attention or mood. The indispensable set includes phenylalanine; tyrosine is not an indispensable amino acid.

LA lowering and EPA/DHA addition are a combined exposure; not evidence that LA reduction alone causes benefit. AEA was not lowered; within-arm AEA rose in both low-LA groups. Power targeted fatty-acid composition; unbalanced allocation, recruitment stopped early and last measurements carried forward. No inflammation, brain signalling or clinical efficacy claim.

canonical_relationships.limitations: Neuronal ion-manipulation experiments establish physiological capacity, not oral magnesium delivery at a pharmacological concentration, treatment of excitotoxic injury or benefit above adequacy. Original one-per-subunit wording is retained in history rather than used as dietary stoichiometry.

canonical_relationships.scope: Catalytic metal in mitochondrial manganese superoxide dismutase
canonical_relationships.limitations: Human SOD2 requires manganese; dietary depletion experiments measured lower heart and kidney MnSOD activity in rats. This establishes a bounded enzyme-capacity dependency, not a human dose recommendation, universal tissue response, measured net ROS balance or benefit above adequate intake.

canonical_relationships.scope: SOD2 cofactor for post-generation superoxide dismutation; adjacent protective biology, not evidence of source-specific electron-leak regulation.

canonical_relationships.scope: Dietary manganese supplies the catalytic metal for mitochondrial SOD2; appropriate metal occupancy sustains a local protective capacity and avoids the experimentally observed iron-substituted prooxidant state.
canonical_relationships.limitations: Capacity is supported by protein biochemistry and mouse dietary manipulation; no general-population limitation, extra-intake benefit or human supplement dose is established.

canonical_relationships.scope: Direct amino-acid substrate for MAT-dependent SAMe formation
canonical_relationships.limitations: No ordinary-diet human dose-response demonstrating increased MAT-dependent SAMe synthesis was identified.

canonical_relationships.scope: Amino acid that enters the methionine cycle and is regenerated when homocysteine is remethylated
canonical_relationships.limitations: Methionine is required to enter the cycle. This does not show that raising methionine intake increases human remethylation or transsulfuration rates.

canonical_relationships.scope: Methionine enters the methionine cycle, producing homocysteine that supplies the CBS reaction and carries sulfur into cysteine formation.
canonical_relationships.limitations: Supported upstream supply, not direct CBS substrate or established sulfur-pool limitation. Cysteine is the product of this PM and is not admitted as an additional supply input. Tissue allocation, compensation and benefit from extra methionine intake are not established.

canonical_relationships.scope: Dietary methionine can supply cysteine for glutathione assembly. Methionine is not a substrate of the assembly enzymes.
canonical_relationships.limitations: A formula that removed methionine and cysteine together slowed whole-blood synthesis, so that result does not isolate methionine. In the cysteine-free study, methionine intake stayed adequate and red-cell synthesis did not fall. This does not show that eating more methionine, once intake is adequate, raises glutathione synthesis.

canonical_relationships.scope: Dietary methionine supplies SAM through MAT-dependent activation, sustaining methyl-donor capacity for PEMT methylation of phosphatidylethanolamine.
canonical_relationships.limitations: Endogenous remethylation also supplies methionine. Neonatal-piglet isotope incorporation does not establish an adult intake target, cerebral delivery or benefit above adequacy. Methyl allocation, SAH inhibition, transport and other substrate availability constrain the route; no shared KC admission follows.

canonical_relationships.scope: Methionine supplies SAM used for COQ3/COQ5 methyl-group transfer.
canonical_relationships.limitations: Capacity admission only: no CoQ-specific intake target, rate limitation under adequate nutrition, increased synthesis from extra intake, mitochondrial delivery or clinical benefit is established.

canonical_relationships.scope: Dietary methionine supplies SAM through MAT-dependent activation, sustaining methyl-donor capacity for GAMT methylation of guanidinoacetate.
canonical_relationships.limitations: Endogenous remethylation also supplies methionine. incomplete_derived_links.scope: Provides methionine through protein digestion and amino-acid absorption; methionine is the direct amino-acid substrate for MAT-dependent SAMe synthesis.
incomplete_derived_links.limitations: Dietary protein provides digestible methionine, but this does not establish that increasing protein or methionine intake increases MAT-dependent SAMe synthesis in humans. DIAAS evaluates sulfur amino acids as methionine + cysteine.

incomplete_derived_links.scope: Provides digestible methionine, the amino acid that enters the cycle.
incomplete_derived_links.limitations: Dietary protein supplies methionine. It does not show that eating more protein increases cycle rates. DIAAS scores sulfur amino acids as methionine plus cysteine.

canonical_relationships.scope: Supplemental cysteine precursor given with glycine to older adults, in whom erythrocyte glutathione synthesis increased.
canonical_relationships.limitations: The synthesis increase was measured in older adults given this precursor together with glycine. It does not show an effect of N-acetylcysteine alone, of ordinary foods, or of supplementation outside that group, and it is not a neuronal or clinical result.

network_relationships.limitation: The synthesis increase was measured in older adults given this precursor together with glycine. It does not show an effect of N-acetylcysteine alone, of ordinary foods, or of supplementation outside that group, and it is not a neuronal or clinical result.

remaining_target_gaps.hold: The admitted exposure is supplemental NAC combined with glycine. Ordinary-food ranking is not appropriate to this protocol; retain the admission and trial limitations.

canonical_relationships.scope: Oxidised NAD is the intracellular cofactor pool supplied by the separately admitted precursor route.
canonical_relationships.limitations: This is a biochemical cofactor target, not an independent oral target admission or food-content claim.

network_relationships.route: derived intervention target; not direct dietary admission
network_relationships.limitation: An established intracellular route is not proof that all oral NR reaches each tissue intact; parallel degradation/salvage can contribute. NMNAT1 establishes reaction identity; other isoforms/transport determine compartmental provision. No fixed dietary conversion yield or mitochondrial/brain endpoint is inferred.

path.process: Human NRK1 phosphorylates beta-NR to beta-NMN using ATP.
path.limitations: An established intracellular route is not proof that all oral NR reaches each tissue intact; parallel degradation/salvage can contribute.

evidence.statement: NRK1 curated reaction, entry version 170, Rhea 14017, retrieved 26 October 2026.

path.process: NMN adenylyltransferase adenylates oxidised beta-NMN with ATP to form oxidised NAD.

canonical_relationships.scope: Nicotinamide is the salvage substrate that NAMPT recycles toward NAD⁺.
canonical_relationships.limitations: The review identifies the salvage substrate. It does not show that eating more nicotinamide, once intake is adequate, raises NAD⁺. The myopathy niacin study used nicotinic acid at pharmacological doses.

network_relationships.limitation: The review identifies the salvage substrate. It does not show that eating more nicotinamide, once intake is adequate, raises NAD⁺. The myopathy niacin study used nicotinic acid at pharmacological doses.

incomplete_derived_links.scope: The liver can convert tryptophan to nicotinamide, which other cells salvage into NAD⁺.
incomplete_derived_links.limitations: Most cells outside the liver do not run the full route. The review does not establish what share of the NAD⁺ pool comes from tryptophan, and eating more protein is not shown to raise NAD⁺.

canonical_relationships.scope: Dietary nicotinamide riboside can supply the NAD precursor pool through supported salvage reactions, sustaining NAD-availability capacity.

Intestinal metabolism and tissue salvage can differ from the displayed intracellular NRK route; other NAD precursors remain alternatives.

canonical_relationships.scope: Phenylalanine is hydroxylated to tyrosine in peripheral tissues, replenishing the circulating tyrosine available to [LAT1 transport](/docs/biological-targets/brs1/fm1/brs1-fm1-pm2-lat1-competitive-transport-modulation) upstream of dopamine synthesis.
canonical_relationships.limitations: Human peripheral conversion supplies circulating tyrosine; neuronal delivery uses the separately supported transport chain. This does not establish increased dopamine/noradrenaline output, a limiting intake or benefit from extra phenylalanine. Hydroxylation, renal/hepatic function and LNAA competition matter; high phenylalanine is not interchangeable with tyrosine.

Single3-g choline challenge, not ordinary egg consumption or a daily dose recommendation; lower-dose effect may differ. No plasma phospholipid-DHA response; no between-drink TAG-DHA difference after dose correction. Do not claim DHA superiority. Plasma concentration/iAUC is not measured absorption fraction, brain choline, acetylcholine synthesis or cognition. 37 g isolated egg phospholipids in a defined drink, not37 g egg yolk; whole-food equivalence untested. Specific causal mediator unresolved; omit a collapsed mechanism summary pending adequate identification.

canonical_relationships.scope: Resistant starch supplies colonic microbes whose fermentation products contribute upstream to epithelial barrier biology.
canonical_relationships.limitations: Response varies with starch type, preparation, dose and microbiota. Faecal short-chain fatty acids do not measure epithelial delivery or establish human tight-junction improvement; resistant potato starch results do not establish effects for every RS2 or RS3 preparation.

canonical_relationships.scope: These resistant starch forms provide substrates for specialist microbial degradation and cross-feeding; adding Ruminococcus bromii enhanced RS3 fermentation in one donor’s faecal community in vitro.
canonical_relationships.limitations: Cultures and one donor’s faecal rescue do not establish oral R. bromii efficacy, uniform human processing, equivalence to RS4 or clinical benefit.

canonical_relationships.scope: Resistant starch reaching the colon supplies fermentable carbohydrate to microbial communities capable of its utilisation, supporting SCFA-production capacity.
canonical_relationships.limitations: Utilisation and product distribution depend on starch structure, processing, accessibility, primary degraders and cross-feeding partners. Evidence for one formulation does not establish an equivalent butyrate response from another preparation or whole food. No predictable yield, intake target or brain benefit is established.

canonical_relationships.scope: Defined oral resistant-starch supplementation modulated clamp-measured insulin sensitivity and post-meal forearm glucose clearance in a small human study.
canonical_relationships.limitations: Preparation-, dose- and population-specific. The positive study used 30 g/day for four weeks in ten healthy participants; this is not an effective whole-food dose. Preserve the later 40 g/day type-2-diabetes null. SCFA mediation and universal benefit are unestablished; no brain or ADHD inference.

canonical_relationships.scope: Selenocysteine source for glutathione peroxidase, which clears hydroperoxides
canonical_relationships.limitations: In selenium-deficient adults, plasma glutathione peroxidase activity levelled off once intake reached about 35 micrograms a day. Intake above that plateau did not raise the enzyme further, and the study did not measure net oxidative pressure.

canonical_relationships.scope: Dietary selenium supplies the selenocysteine-dependent phospholipid-hydroperoxide glutathione-peroxidase capacity that removes membrane lipid hydroperoxides.
canonical_relationships.limitations: Mouse whole-organ enzyme assays do not identify mitochondrial isoforms, a human food dose or benefit above selenium adequacy. Repletion response depended on dose; antioxidant capacity does not establish clinical prevention.

canonical_relationships.scope: Dietary selenium supplies selenocysteine-dependent thioredoxin-reductase capacity for regeneration of reduced thioredoxin.
canonical_relationships.limitations: Culture selenium exposure is not an oral food dose. This supports the thioredoxin arm, not selenium dependence of glutathione reductase, universal tissue recycling flux or benefit above adequacy.

canonical_relationships.scope: Modulates KEAP1-mediated control of Nrf2, promoting antioxidant-response gene transcription. Human dietary exposure increased Nrf2-associated phase II enzyme RNA in nasal lavage cells.
canonical_relationships.limitations: Human target engagement varies by formulation, tissue and population. The positive study used a myrosinase-completed broccoli sprout homogenate for three days in healthy nonsmokers and measured nasal phase II enzyme RNA, not Nrf2 protein or nuclear translocation. Extract capsules did not increase lung target-gene expression in COPD. An ordinary broccoli meal, direct activation of Nrf2 in the human brain and clinical ADHD benefit remain unestablished. Sulforaphane is not an essential nutrient.

available_food_evidence.id: broccoli::sulforaphane::uk mature broccoli sous vide at 100 c for 20 minutes with and without 1 g brown mustard powder::raw
available_food_evidence.material: UK mature broccoli, sous vide at 100 °C for 20 minutes, with and without 1 g brown mustard powder

presence_records.evidence: Okunade, Niranjan, Ghawi, Kuhnle and Methven (2018), Molecular Nutrition & Food Research 62:1700980. Formation identity also rests on Fahey et al. (1997).
presence_records.limitations: Sulforaphane forms from glucoraphanin when myrosinase is active. In one cooked-broccoli study the amount depended on preparation, and it is not entered as a per-100 g nutrient.

presence_records.label: Sulforaphane
presence_records.public_note: One UK broccoli lot, cooked sous vide at 100 °C for 20 minutes, formed 1.06 µmol sulforaphane per g dry weight. Adding 1 g brown mustard powder raised that to 8.58 µmol/g dry weight. Twelve adults who ate 200 g excreted 9.8 µmol sulforaphane-NAC per g creatinine in 24 hours, and 44.7 µmol/g creatinine with the mustard. These figures are not a sulforaphane amount for every 100 g of broccoli.
presence_records.source_note: Okunade et al. (2018), Molecular Nutrition & Food Research 62:1700980, Table 1 and the 24-hour urine result. Table 1, µmol sulforaphane per g dry weight: raw 2.05 ± 0.25; sous vide 100 °C for 20 minutes 1.06 ± 0.18; the same cooked broccoli plus 1 g brown mustard powder 8.58 ± 0.33. 8.58 / 1.06 = 8.1, which the paper reports as an 8-fold increase. One results sentence prints the mustard result as 8.58 ± 0.13; the table figure is used here. Urine, 12 adults, 200 g of that cooked broccoli: 9.8 ± 5.1 µmol sulforaphane-NAC per g creatinine in 24 hours without mustard, and 44.7 ± 33.9 with 1 g mustard. 44.7 / 9.8 = 4.6 from the published means. The paper's average of each person's increase is 4.7-fold, with individual increases from 1.7-fold to 10-fold. Sous-vide myrosinase loss in the same paper: 40% after 2 minutes, 90% after 6 minutes, and no measurable activity after 8 minutes. The study did not report a glucoraphanin concentration, and the dry-weight results are not converted to a fresh 100 g amount. Fahey et al. (1997) identifies sulforaphane as the myrosinase product of glucoraphanin; it is not the source of these figures.

calculation.not_a_panel_amount: Dry-weight and creatinine-normalised study results. No moisture figure is given, so they are not scaled to per 100 g fresh broccoli.

canonical_relationships.scope: Indispensable serotonergic precursor this PM prioritises in the circulating precursor pool
canonical_relationships.limitations: Pool presence of tryptophan is not evidence for increased brain serotonin, brain entry, or an attention or mood benefit.

canonical_relationships.scope: Large-neutral amino acid that competes for LAT1-mediated brain entry
canonical_relationships.limitations: Meal-driven changes in plasma tryptophan-to-LNAA ratios do not establish increased brain serotonin or a clinical benefit.

canonical_relationships.scope: Substrate for tryptophan hydroxylase conversion to 5-hydroxytryptophan, the immediate precursor of serotonin
canonical_relationships.limitations: Substrate necessity does not establish that additional dietary tryptophan increases brain serotonin or improves mood, sleep or ADHD.

canonical_relationships.scope: The liver can convert tryptophan to nicotinamide, which other cells salvage into NAD⁺.
canonical_relationships.limitations: Most cells outside the liver do not run the full route. The review does not establish what share of the NAD⁺ pool comes from tryptophan, and eating more protein is not shown to raise NAD⁺.

canonical_relationships.scope: Immediate substrate used by the microbial tryptophan-processing routes assessed here.
canonical_relationships.limitations: Substrate participation is not benefit from increased intake; host absorption, endogenous competition and microbial compartmentation differ from brain precursor delivery.

canonical_relationships.scope: Tryptophan is the dietary precursor of serotonin, and serotonin is the substrate for melatonin formation. Severe depletion lowered nocturnal melatonin secretion.
canonical_relationships.limitations: Depletion shows a constraint. It does not show that extra dietary tryptophan raises melatonin. BRS1 admission is not inherited.

network_relationships.limitation: Pool presence of tryptophan is not evidence for increased brain serotonin, brain entry, or an attention or mood benefit.

canonical_relationships.scope: Catecholamine precursor in the circulating pool this PM prioritises. Tyrosine is normally formed from indispensable phenylalanine and can become conditionally indispensable when phenylalanine availability is limited
canonical_relationships.limitations: Dietary supply to a circulating pool is distinct from brain transport, catecholamine synthesis or clinical benefit. A small human study found higher plasma tyrosine during protein-containing meals and after a large tyrosine supplement; it does not define ordinary-food efficacy or a need for extra tyrosine when supply is adequate. Tyrosine is not an indispensable amino acid.

canonical_relationships.scope: Large-neutral amino acid that competes for LAT1-mediated brain entry
canonical_relationships.limitations: Competitive transport biology does not establish that eating more tyrosine increases brain tyrosine or catecholamine signalling.

canonical_relationships.scope: Tyrosine is the substrate for conversion to L-DOPA in dopamine synthesis.
canonical_relationships.limitations: Substrate necessity does not establish that additional dietary tyrosine increases brain dopamine or improves a functional or clinical outcome.

canonical_relationships.scope: The reviewed LNAA pool presents tyrosine through [BRS1 PM2 — LAT1 transport](/docs/biological-targets/brs1/fm1/brs1-fm1-pm2-lat1-competitive-transport-modulation) for synthesis of dopamine, the immediate precursor converted by DBH into noradrenaline.
canonical_relationships.limitations: Tyrosine is upstream precursor supply, not the immediate DBH substrate or an independently adjudicated Direct dietary requirement here. Ordinary dietary competitive changes do not establish a limiting effect on regional noradrenergic signalling or benefit from extra tyrosine.

canonical_relationships.scope: Tyrosine supplies quinone-head carbon through the HPDL-associated 4-HMA/4-HB pathway.
canonical_relationships.limitations: Capacity admission only: no CoQ-specific intake target, rate limitation under adequate nutrition, increased synthesis from extra intake, mitochondrial delivery or clinical benefit is established. Endogenous phenylalanine conversion is an alternative source; the full human intervening enzyme sequence remains incompletely assigned.

canonical_relationships.scope: Uridine can supply CTP used in CDP-choline and phosphatidylcholine formation, contributing membrane precursors for structural assembly.
canonical_relationships.limitations: Endogenous nucleotide synthesis and salvage also contribute. UMP alone did not significantly increase gerbil spine density; that null structural result does not erase the precursor role. No ordinary-food dose or human structural benefit is established.

canonical_relationships.scope: Uridine can be converted through nucleotide metabolism into CTP, which helps form the CDP-choline used to build phosphatidylcholine.
canonical_relationships.limitations: Uridine is a supported precursor source, not an indispensable dietary requirement: endogenous nucleotide synthesis and salvage also supply CTP. Rat-slice and oral-UMP gerbil results do not establish an ordinary-food dose, increased human PC flux or cognitive benefit; human MRS measures precursor pools.

network_relationships.limitation: Endogenous nucleotide synthesis and salvage also contribute. UMP alone did not significantly increase gerbil spine density; that null structural result does not erase the precursor role. No ordinary-food dose or human structural benefit is established.

canonical_relationships.scope: Riboflavin supplies FMN and FAD used by methionine-synthase reductase to regenerate active B12-dependent methionine synthase.
canonical_relationships.limitations: Foundational human-enzyme cofactor provenance supports capacity; it is not a measurement of dietary riboflavin-induced remethylation flux, brain methylation or benefit above adequacy. FMN is also required; FAD is the endpoint of the displayed activation chain, not its sole functional cofactor.

canonical_relationships.limitations: Riboflavin supports formation of the methyl donor. It is not the cofactor at the methionine-synthase catalytic site, and it has not been shown to change human cycle rates.

canonical_relationships.scope: Supplies riboflavin for endogenous FMN and FAD synthesis; FAD supports glutathione reductase regeneration of reduced glutathione.
canonical_relationships.limitations: Human red-cell enzyme evidence supports flavin-dependent capacity. It does not establish neuronal or whole-body recycling flux, benefit above adequacy, or equivalence between an ordinary food and a 5 mg/day supplement.

canonical_relationships.scope: Riboflavin is the vitamin precursor of flavin mononucleotide (FMN), the flavin that accepts NADH electrons in complex I.
canonical_relationships.limitations: The review does not show that eating more riboflavin, once flavin mononucleotide (FMN) is adequate, raises electron transport. Riboflavin-responsive complex I disease is a separate clinical context.

canonical_relationships.limitations: Dietary B6 can supply PLP precursors, including vitamers that enter the central nervous system, but increasing B6 intake has not been shown to increase human brain dopamine synthesis.

canonical_relationships.scope: Provides dietary B6 vitamers that pyridoxal kinase converts to PLP, the cofactor required for GAD-dependent GABA synthesis
canonical_relationships.limitations: Dietary B6 provision of PLP precursors is supported, but increasing B6 intake has not been shown to increase human brain GABA synthesis; PLP supports many enzymes and is not GABA-specific.

canonical_relationships.scope: Provides pyridoxal phosphate, the cofactor for the transsulfuration exit that converts homocysteine toward cysteine
canonical_relationships.limitations: In nine healthy young adults, 28 days of vitamin B6 restriction lowered plasma pyridoxal phosphate and did not change mean postprandial remethylation, transmethylation, or total transsulfuration rates.

canonical_relationships.scope: Food source of the pyridoxal 5'-phosphate cofactor used by cystathionine beta-synthase and cystathionine gamma-lyase, through the vitamin B6 salvage pathway.
canonical_relationships.limitations: Salvage of food vitamin B6 to pyridoxal 5'-phosphate does not show that higher vitamin B6 intake increases cystathionine beta-synthase or cystathionine gamma-lyase flux. Moderate B6 restriction changed cystathionine handling but did not significantly reduce total transsulfuration in the assessed human tracer study.

canonical_relationships.scope: Folate supplies the methyl group through [BRS2 PM1 — Folate/B12 remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm1-folate-b12-dependent-homocysteine-remethylation), replenishing methionine used by [BRS2 PM3 — MAT/SAM synthesis](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm3-same-synthesis). SAM is the methyl donor used by COMT during dopamine metabolism.
canonical_relationships.limitations: This requires functional B12-dependent remethylation. The connected reaction chain does not measure dietary folate contribution to regional brain SAM or clearance; alternative methionine supply and tissue turnover matter. A limiting effect and benefit from extra intake remain unresolved.

canonical_relationships.scope: Folate-dependent methyl metabolism helps maintain the brain choline resource available for acetylcholine formation; folate deprivation lowered choline and acetylcholine in studied mouse models, with SAM rescue supporting this upstream resource relationship.
canonical_relationships.limitations: Animal evidence is conditional on age, brain region and experimental context. Choline and acetylcholine concentrations were measured; methyl-dependent choline retention and the consequence for synthesis capacity are mechanistic inferences, not measured human synthesis flux. Folate is not a ChAT cofactor; extra folate above adequacy and cognitive benefit are not established.

canonical_relationships.scope: Folate-derived one-carbon units support [BRS2 PM1 — remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm1-folate-b12-dependent-homocysteine-remethylation), replenishing methionine for SAM-dependent [BRS2 PM7 — PEMT formation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm3/brs2-fm3-pm7-phosphatidylcholine-formation), upstream of DHA-bearing LPC carrier delivery.
canonical_relationships.limitations: Supported biochemical supply chain, not a demonstrated increase in net adult brain DHA incorporation. Folate/choline compensation, hepatic BHMT, SAM turnover and carrier remodelling vary by context. Mouse folate effects were sex/tissue dependent; betaine rescue used ethanol-exposed rats. The downstream human tracer study administered choline, not folate or betaine. A donor-specific limiting effect and extra-intake benefit remain unresolved.

canonical_relationships.scope: Dietary folate, including folic acid reduced by dihydrofolate reductase, is converted through the folate cycle to 5-methyltetrahydrofolate, the methyl donor used by methionine synthase.
canonical_relationships.limitations: This conversion pathway does not show that increasing folate intake increases tissue remethylation flux. Folic acid lowers blood homocysteine, which is a circulating marker.

canonical_relationships.scope: Folate supplies 5-methyltetrahydrofolate to [PM1 — Folate/B12-dependent remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm1-folate-b12-dependent-homocysteine-remethylation), regenerating methionine that PM3 can use to form SAMe.
canonical_relationships.limitations: This is upstream methionine supply, not a MAT substrate or cofactor. The route depends on functional vitamin B12-dependent methionine synthase; alternative methionine supply and tissue context affect its contribution. Increased MAT flux or benefit from extra folate in replete individuals is not established.

canonical_relationships.limitations: Folic acid can lower blood homocysteine concentration. That concentration change is not a measured change in remethylation or transsulfuration rate.
